title: photowright: name, repo, Photoshop bridge, first projects

questions.title: Plugin name
questions.question: Which name should the image editing and vectorizing plugin ship under?
questions.background: The plugin does Photoshop-like edits and traces images to vectors from the command line. The working name is photowright; rasterwright was the other candidate.
questions.why: The name goes into the repo, the skill names and the script docs, and changing it after release is costly.

guess.why: Says what people will ask for (photo edits); vectorizing still fits under it.

questions.title: Public or private
questions.question: When should the photowright repository become public?
questions.background: It is private now at m4bwav/photowright, like most new plugins before their first release.
questions.why: Public repos get a wiki, banner and directory-style release; private ones build on the local runner.

options.label: Make it public at the first release

guess.why: Same path as mapwright and fractalwright.

questions.title: Photoshop bridge
questions.question: Should photowright include an optional Photoshop bridge at all?
questions.background: Everything is built on free tools and the plugin's own code first. A bridge would hand a recipe to Photoshop through its scripting interface when it is installed. It would be off by default, and no feature would depend on it.
questions.why: If no, the bridge step is dropped and the release comes sooner.

options.label: Yes, early: I use Photoshop often

guess.why: You said Photoshop is optional; building it last keeps the free path complete first.

questions.title: Photoshop version
questions.question: Which Photoshop version do you have installed, if any?
questions.background: The bridge works differently for each version (UXP, ExtendScript or COM on Windows).

guess.why: No Photoshop install was found here.

questions.title: First real jobs
questions.question: Which of your projects should the first real test jobs come from?
questions.background: Before release, the plugin does four real jobs: a photo retouch, a layered composite, a batch over a folder, and a trace to a clean vector.
questions.why: These jobs become the acceptance tests, so they should be work you would keep.

guess.why: Both have lots of game art that needs traces and batch edits.

questions.title: Install desktop tools
questions.question: May the session install Potrace, Inkscape and GIMP to compare against and to check layered files?
questions.background: Today only VTracer (pip, MIT) and the plugin's own tracers were measured. To check that a written PSD opens correctly, the file has to be opened in GIMP or Krita.
questions.why: If yes, the layered-file checks and the Potrace comparison run for real. If no, they are skipped and marked unverified.

guess.why: All three are free and open source, and the proof bars need GIMP or Krita.
